items.title: We are yet to decide on validity of logical discrepancy in SIR: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court orally said on Wednesday that it has not rendered any final decision on the validity of Election Commission of India (ECI) employing 'logical discrepancy' to weed out electors in its special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in various States. While the Court had earlier upheld the validity of SIR exercise in Bihar, the Court today said that the logical discrepancy issue was not decided in that matter. The Court had later permitted ECI to employ 'logical discrepancy' prior to the West Bengal assembly polls but the same was only an interim measure and not a final decision, the apex court said today. The remarks were made by a bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana after the ECI counsel argued today that the apex court has examined every step of SIR and upheld it. "Ever since the SIR process was initiated, Your Lordships have been seized of the matter and have examined every step. Your Lordships may recall what happened in Bihar," the counsel said.
